comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the core fix is sound. `feature_disable=0x82000` masks brcmfmac FWSUP (bit 13) and SAE (bit 19). With either masked, the driver stops advertising `SAE_OFFLOAD`, and wpa_supplicant then drops every SAE key management option, which produces the "Failed to select authenticated key management type" error in the PR description. Removing the quirk from BCM4364 and Apple Silicon (`4425`/`4433`) follows from that source, and the corrected comment (SAE, not FWAUTH) is accurate. In isolated runs with stubbed hardware, the new install gate, the edited `1786391100.sh` and the new cleanup behave as described for unmodified files: exact Omarchy blocks are removed, preceding user lines are kept byte for byte, `reboot-required` is set before the edit and only when something changes, administrator-merged options lines are left alone, symlinks are written through, and an unreadable file fails the migration so it is retried. Both PR test suites pass on the head and fail on the base code for the intended reasons.

Two issues and one test gap remain.

### Cleanup silently skips an Omarchy block that has lines after it

`migrations/1790165000.sh` accepts the legacy T2 block only as the whole file and the current block only as the end of the file. On a T2 or BCM4364 Mac where a user later appended anything after the Omarchy block, the migration exits 0 without editing:

| Start file on T2 + `14e4:4464` | Result | Effective brcmfmac options after |
|---|---|---|
| Omarchy block only | block removed, reboot requested | driver defaults |
| user line, then Omarchy block | block removed, user line kept | user line only |
| Omarchy block, then `options brcmfmac roamoff=1` | no edit, no reboot, migration marked done | `feature_disable=0x82000 roamoff=1` |
| Omarchy block, then a comment | no edit, no reboot, migration marked done | `feature_disable=0x82000` |

(Effective options are derived from kmod and kernel parameter-parsing source, not from running `modprobe`.)

No Omarchy writer puts content after its block. The installers overwrite the file, and the old migration appends its block at the end. This shape therefore comes from a later user edit, such as `sudo tee -a` or an editor. On T2 Macs, which received the block at install time, any later customization lands in exactly this position.

**Impact:** for those users, WPA3-only networks keep failing, while the update prints "Restore WPA3 support on Broadcom BCM4364 and Apple Silicon Macs". `omarchy-migrate` marks the migration done, so it is not retried. `feature_disable` is not exposed in sysfs, so the leftover quirk is hard to spot.

**Suggested change:** remove either exact Omarchy block wherever it appears on whole-line boundaries, keeping all other bytes. Any `feature_disable=` value an administrator added after the block already overrides it, so this never changes an administrator-set value. A disposable variant doing this still passed all 8 assertions in `brcmfmac-wpa3-cleanup-test.sh` and left administrator-merged and reworded variants untouched. Add a cleanup test with a user line after the block to pin the chosen behavior.

### Not every T2 Mac carries BCM4364

The description and comments say every T2 Intel Mac has BCM4364, and they list `43dc` and `4488` as legacy pre-T2 parts. The kernel's `brcm_hw_ids.h` and the commits that added these IDs to brcmfmac say otherwise:

| PCI ID | PR label | brcmfmac identity | Documented Macs | Head behavior |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `14e4:43dc` | "BCM43555", legacy pre-T2 | BCM4355 (commit 69005e67ce54) | MacBookAir8,1, 8,2 (T2) | quirk no longer written; existing block removed on upgrade |
| `14e4:4488` | "BCM4355", legacy pre-T2 | BCM4377 (commit bf8bbd903f07) | MacBookPro15,4, 16,3, MacBookAir9,1 (T2) | quirk no longer written; existing block removed on upgrade |

**Impact:** the PR also removes the quirk from these five T2 models, but its hardware evidence covers only BCM4364 (MacBookPro15,2 and 16,1). With the new T2 exclusion, the `43dc` and `4488` entries in the legacy list match no documented Mac.

**Context:** the removal is plausibly correct on these models too. The t2linux Wi-Fi guide recommends this exact `feature_disable=0x82000` as a workaround for a wpa_supplicant 2.11 regression (hostap commit 41638606) that broke brcmfmac WPA2-PSK and WPA3-SAE. Arch's `wpa_supplicant 2:2.12-1` (August 10, 2026) reverts that commit. That history points to a fixed supplicant, not newer firmware, as the likely reason driver defaults now work across T2 radios. It remains untested on BCM4355 and BCM4377 hardware.

**Suggested change:** correct the chip names in the description, the installer comment and the test comment. Drop `43dc` and `4488` from the legacy list, or explain why they stay. State that BCM4355 and BCM4377 T2 Macs also lose the quirk and why, citing the wpa_supplicant history, and ideally confirm on one of them: `iw phy` should show `SAE_OFFLOAD`, then join a WPA3-only and a transition AP.

**Optional test improvement:** every T2 case in both suites uses `4464`, which the Wi-Fi ID lists already handle without the T2 check. Deleting the `106b:180[12]` exclusion from the installer, from `1786391100.sh` or from the cleanup gate left each suite passing. Adding `T2_HARDWARE=1` cases with `4488` or `43dc` (no quirk written, old migration skips, cleanup removes an existing block) would catch that.

**Documentation note:** `migrations/1786391100.sh` still says T2 installs already carry the quirk from the installer, which no longer holds.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** source review of the PR, `bin/omarchy-migrate` and `bin/omarchy-update`, and dependency source: Linux brcmfmac (mainline, v7.1 and stable 7.1.8), wpa_supplicant 2.12, NetworkManager and kmod. Isolated command-only runs with stubbed `lspci`, `sudo` and `omarchy-state` and redirected config paths covered an installer matrix, upgrade sequences through the real migration runner, cleanup edge cases, the PR test suites on head and base, and deliberate deletions of the T2 check. No Apple or Broadcom hardware was available. Association behavior is inferred from source and the PR's reported live tests, not reproduced.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments with targeted follow-up questions, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
